page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, running on an Intel x86_64 processor. The hardware configuration consists of 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8), and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but overall weak to poor multi-core and memory performance. Single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests place the instance in the average tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0 and a gzip compression throughput of 28.28 GB/sec. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core (1714.68) and Geekbench multi-core (2251.0), fall into the weak and poor categories. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block read and write speeds recorded at 19.35 GB/sec and 12.78 GB/sec respectively.

From a workload perspective, the n4-standard-2 is suitable for lightweight general-purpose tasks, basic text processing, and single-threaded applications. It exhibits weak performance in database operations, software compilation, and LLM inference, making it less suitable for resource-intensive or highly parallelized workloads. Given its dedicated CPU allocation and standard resource density, it offers a predictable entry-level option for workloads that do not require high memory bandwidth or local SSD storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine configured with 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads, it features dedicated CPU allocation and a 260 MB L3 cache. The architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs. Benchmark results show average single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0, but weak multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. Consequently, the n4-standard-2 is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and low-intensity web serving, rather than demanding database operations or parallelized computing tasks.
